shared_elements: upright slab/pillar with a broader head element (T-shape) bearing carvings on its broad face
low-relief motifs arranged in vertical/stacked registers
animal forms in profile within the field
narrow vertical bands or strips running down the sides of the shaft
small repeated elements arranged in a row/band
justification: Both surfaces are the broad face of an upright, T-headed slab covered with shallow, flat-relief motifs stacked in registers, with narrow vertical strips framing the sides and animal figures in profile occupying the central field, and both share the same low-relief, schematic, silhouette-with-minimal-interior-detail convention. The difference is in the legible content: A shows a clear, densely populated menagerie (rows of small animals, a netted band, quadrupeds, snakes and a large long-necked bird) whereas B's field is dominated by a few large, elongated abstract or object-like vertical forms with only one or two ambiguous creatures, so no single distinctive motif can be matched between them.
